hook: $11.99 fairy lights beat a $16 sconce for glow

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of a single plug-in sconce casting a small pool of light on a wall
scenes.on_screen_text: One sconce = one wall's worth of glow
scenes.voiceover: A single sconce covers about one wall's worth of ambient light. That's it.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of 33ft warm-white fairy lights wrapped three times around a large console mirror
scenes.voiceover: For basically the same price, 33 feet of warm-white string lights wraps a whole mirror frame two or three times.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of the plug adaptor going into a wall outlet, not batteries
scenes.on_screen_text: Plugs in. No dead batteries mid-evening.
scenes.voiceover: It plugs into the wall, so it's not dying on you halfway through the evening like the battery versions do.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text overlay showing star rating and review count: 4.5 stars, 13,028 ratings
scenes.voiceover: Over thirteen thousand ratings sit at 4.5 stars — that's a big enough sample to trust.

scenes.visual_prompt: Full room shot: console table, mirror wrapped in lights, small lamp, cozy fall styling
scenes.on_screen_text: This is the 'cozy corner' photo you're searching for
scenes.voiceover: This is the shot that's actually behind most of those 'cozy bedroom lighting' searches — not the sconce alone.

scenes.visual_prompt: Side-by-side comparison card: Sconce $16 one wall vs Fairy lights $11.99 whole mirror
scenes.voiceover: Same budget, more coverage — that's the trade worth knowing before you buy.

caption: I compared what a $16 plug-in sconce actually covers versus $11.99 in warm-white string lights — same price range, very different coverage. 13,028 ratings back this one up. Full comparison on the blog, link in bio.
